Docs.param: The fully-qualified DNS name or IP address of the endpoint. Traffic Manager returns this value in DNS responses to direct traffic to this endpoint.

Monitoring target is where Private Traffic Manager will gather health information.It can differ from the endpoint target, for example when the target is an IPv6 address. If not configured, the endpoint target is used. It is required when the target is IPv6 and cannot itself be an IPv6 address.
The status of the endpoint. If the endpoint is Enabled, it is probed for endpoint health and is included in the traffic routing method.
The weight of this endpoint when using the 'Weighted' traffic routing method. Possible values are from 1 to 1000.

The priority of this endpoint when using the 'Priority' traffic routing method. Possible values are from 1 to 1000, lower values represent higher priority. This is an optional parameter. If specified, it must be specified on all endpoints, and no two endpoints can share the same priority value.
Indicates whether endpoint is Always Serve or not. Always Serve endpoints are always considered to be healthy.
The health policy associated with this endpoint.

The virtual network ARM resource IDs assigned to this endpoint when using the 'VNet' traffic routing method. A virtual network must not be assigned to more than one endpoint in the profile. A profile can have at most one fallback endpoint; an endpoint with no virtual networks is that fallback.
